metaDesc: The 10 most popular restaurants in Roi Et 2026 that locals keep coming back to — from Tam Kratoei Sagate and HED-Het to Sam Phi Nong's free-range chicken soup, Aew's pan-fried eggs, and a forest café. With zones, signature dishes, and price ranges.

ogTitle: 10 Most Popular Restaurants in Roi Et 2026 — Eat Like a Local
ogDesc: Som tam, laab, free-range chicken soup, congee, pan-fried eggs, and a forest café — the best spots in Roi Et that locals keep returning to, with zones, signature dishes, and price ranges all in one place.
intro: Roi Et is an Isan city where the food is genuinely bold and honest. From roadside som tam stalls to elevated Isan restaurants around Bung Phlan Chai lake, we've gathered the 10 spots that locals keep returning to and travelers mention most — covering breakfast, group dinners, and a café to unwind in, all in a single trip.

blocks.html:
If you had to describe Roi Et as a food lover would, the charm of this city is that Isan food is still the real thing and easy to find in every part of town. In the mornings, locals start the day with hot pan-fried eggs and Vietnamese bread in the city center. Mid-morning they stop for a big-mortar som tam in the north of town. By evening the area around Bung Phlan Chai lake transforms into a gathering spot — newer Isan restaurants showcasing local ingredients alongside riverside garden restaurants where a cool breeze, live music, and a spread of shared dishes make for a genuinely great meal. Walk a few steps and you'll find something completely different. That's the joy of eating in Roi Et.

Many of the restaurants on this list have their own story. Tam Kratoei Sagate started as a small roadside som tam stall in 2014 and grew into an Isan brand with Bangkok branches and a Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition. Tom Kai Ban Sam Phi Nong and Khao Tom Liang Heng have been open for decades and have become the city's defining flavors — generations of families still make the trip. HED-Het is a new-wave Isan restaurant around Bung Phlan Chai that takes local ingredients like red-ant eggs and field crabs and reinvents them brilliantly. Aew Khai Kratha is the go-to breakfast spot with single-digit-to-double-digit prices. Every restaurant on this list is open, has regulars, and is ready for you to try yourself.

blocks.name: Tam Kratoei Sagate (Roi Et)
blocks.area: Nuea Mueang, Mueang Roi Et District, Roi Et
blocks.signature: Tam Luem Phua with boiled egg and duck feet, grilled tilapia, fried chicken wings, pad Thai with fresh prawns
blocks.descHtml:
If you come to Roi Et and skip "Tam Kratoei Sagate," you've missed the city's most iconic restaurant — a legendary som tam spot that started as a small roadside stall in 2014 and grew into an Isan brand with branches across the region. The Roi Et branch is the original and the flagship, located on the ring road behind Phetcharat Hotel. The space is large, parking is easy, and it works well for groups, families, or a first meal after arriving in town.

The dish everyone talks about is "Tam Luem Phua" — a rich Lao-style som tam loaded with boiled egg and duck feet, deep fermented-fish aroma, big crunchy chunks of papaya. Reviews consistently describe it as the kind of dish you can't stop eating. Don't miss the large grilled tilapia either — sweet, springy flesh with two dipping sauces. The crispy fried chicken wings and fresh prawn pad Thai are standouts too, with many guests surprised that a som tam restaurant does pad Thai this well. If you love strong fermented-fish flavor, try the crab-and-pla-ra som tam or the tom som pla kang.

Prices are accessible — som tam from the mid-50s THB, fried wings in the hundreds, the big pla kang soup is easy to share. Per person averages around 150–250 THB. The restaurant has both an air-conditioned section and an open Isan-style outdoor area. Reviewers praise the fast service and consistent flavors across every dish.

The popularity is well-earned. The restaurant holds a 4.4-star Google rating from over a thousand reviews and has received the Michelin Bib Gourmand for multiple consecutive years. Note: weekend evenings get very busy. Arriving before peak hours or calling ahead to book a table is worth the effort.
mustOrder: Tam Luem Phua with boiled egg and duck feet
blocks.bestFor: First meal in Roi Et, groups who love fierce som tam
blocks.spice: Adjustable heat — Lao-style tam is boldly fermented and fiery

blocks.name: HED - Het Roi Et
blocks.area: Around Bung Phlan Chai, Mueang Roi Et District, Roi Et
blocks.signature: Kaeng phak wan khai mot daeng, laab moo thot, pork neck, tom saeb cartilage, Lao-style som tam with field crab and olive
blocks.descHtml:
Ask Roi Et locals where to go for seriously good Isan food and many will point you straight to "Het" (HED) — a small restaurant on Sunthon Thep Road around Bung Phlan Chai, just behind Café HER. The owner, Ann, left Bangkok to return home and open a seasonally driven local-ingredient restaurant, using things like red-ant eggs, field crabs, free-range chicken, river fish, and foraged vegetables prepared in a genuinely traditional Isan style. This is the place for people who want authentic, full-flavored home cooking — not a watered-down version — and it works equally well for lunch with friends or a family meal.

Must-order: kaeng phak wan khai mot daeng (sweet leaf curry with red-ant eggs) — the broth has a subtle fermented-fish warmth that doesn't overwhelm the sweetness of the leaves, and the ant eggs are soft and delicate enough that first-timers find them completely approachable. The Roi Et-style laab is heavy on toasted rice fragrance with just the right heat — ask them to dial back the spice if needed. Laab moo thot, thinly sliced grilled pork neck, tom saeb cartilage, and a Lao-style som tam with field crab and olive are all signature dishes. For something unusual, try the strawberry som tam — reviewers say it's surprisingly addictive. Hot sticky rice rounds everything out.

Prices are friendly — som tam from 50 THB, two people ordering six dishes pay around 550 THB. The décor is simple with charming details, right in the city center by Bung Phlan Chai with easy parking. Open daily around 10:00–20:00. Given how popular it's become, the kaeng phak wan khai mot daeng is made in limited batches each day — arrive on the earlier side to make sure you get it.
mustOrder: Kaeng phak wan khai mot daeng (sweet leaf curry with red-ant eggs)
blocks.bestFor: First meal in Roi Et, groups

blocks.name: Tom Kai Ban Sam Phi Nong
blocks.area: Por Phan, Mueang Roi Et District, Roi Et
blocks.signature: Free-range chicken soup with clear broth scented with lemon basil, grilled chicken, fried chicken, crab-and-pla-ra som tam, battered fried river prawns
blocks.descHtml:
If you're driving into Roi Et on the Chaeng Sanit road and want something that tastes like real Isan home cooking, Tom Kai Ban Sam Phi Nong in Por Phan is where locals point you. This family-run restaurant has been open for decades, focusing on free-range chicken with firm, flavorful meat — perfect for a big shared pot around a table, whether family or a group of friends. The space is open and relaxed in the roadside style; no dress code, just walk in and sit down.

Every table orders the free-range chicken soup — a whole pot brought to the table so you can ladle it yourself. The broth is clear but deeply savory, with lemon basil fragrance rising the moment the pot arrives. Many reviewers say they drink the broth straight until their throats run dry. One chicken can be prepared several ways — simmered, grilled, or fried. For grilled chicken, call ahead to order since the kitchen grills each bird fresh. The fried chicken is crisp and fragrant. The unmissable table pairings are the crab-and-pla-ra som tam, full-flavored and punchy, and the battered fried river prawns with spicy dipping sauce — both perfect alongside a hot bowl of chicken soup.

Prices are easy on the wallet — a small pot of free-range chicken soup starts at just over 100 THB and feeds a crowd. Reviewers consistently rate the value as excellent. The restaurant scored around 4.2 on Google and has appeared on popular local food lists.

Good to know: open daily roughly 08:30–18:00. For grilled chicken, call about an hour ahead. It can get busy on holidays. Being an open-air roadside spot, the occasional fly visits, as you'd expect from an authentic Isan restaurant — but the flavors and atmosphere more than make up for it.
mustOrder: Free-range chicken soup (clear broth with lemon basil)
blocks.bestFor: Groups and families gathering around a big shared pot

blocks.name: Bangkok33
blocks.area: Mueang Roi Et District, Roi Et
blocks.signature: German pork knuckle, grilled river prawns, BBQ pork ribs, salmon steak
blocks.descHtml:
Bangkok33 is a long-established eat-and-drink restaurant on the Chaeng Sanit road before the bypass intersection — the kind of place Roi Et residents head to when they want a long, relaxed evening out. Live music plays every night. The menu is wide, covering Thai food, drinking snacks, Western dishes, and seafood, making it a good fit for groups or families who want food and atmosphere in one place.

Popular orders include a large German pork knuckle with crispy skin and dipping sauce, big grilled river prawns, BBQ pork ribs, and salmon steak. On the Thai side there's deep-fried sea bass with fish sauce, salmon nam phrik set, baked glass-noodle prawns, and wasabi-crab spring rolls as an opener. Guests consistently mention good flavors, friendly service, and how the live music and atmosphere make the evening fly by.

Seating is flexible — five zones including a roadside section, outdoor area, stage-front, and both small and large air-conditioned rooms. Choose based on your group size and how close you want to be to the band. Per person runs around 101–250 THB. Easy parking, credit cards accepted, and pets welcome.

Open daily around 16:00–00:00, focused on dinner through late night. For Friday or Saturday nights, or when a popular band is playing, call ahead to book a table — it fills up fast. Reservations at 099-159-1665.
blocks.bestFor: Evening and late-night out with friends, live music

blocks.name: Khao Tom Liang Heng
blocks.area: Ratchakan Damroen Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Roi Et District, Roi Et
blocks.signature: Chinese-style congee, stir-fried morning glory, nam liap with minced pork, crispy pork, braised bamboo shoots
blocks.descHtml:
Ask the older generation in Roi Et where to go for late-night congee and nearly every answer will be "Liang Heng" — a Chinese-style congee restaurant over 50 years old, right next to the night market on Ratchakan Damroen Road in the city center. Locals have been bringing their families here since their parents' day. If you want a hot bowl of congee, a spread of side dishes across the table, and a long relaxed conversation, this is the answer — great for families arriving late from the road or groups wanting something warm and filling.

Nearly every table orders the Chinese-style congee paired with a selection of side dishes. The stir-fried morning glory with fermented soybean is fragrant and pleasantly salty. Nam liap with minced pork — salty and savory — pairs perfectly with hot congee. The braised bamboo shoots with clear broth is the dish most reviewers say is non-negotiable. There's also crispy pork, red pork, poached fish with dipping sauce, and spicy stir-fried wild boar. Easy to share across a group.

The atmosphere is relaxed in the way a good provincial congee restaurant should be — casual, no dress code. Reviews consistently praise the balanced flavors, fast service, and fair pricing. The location by the night market means you can stroll through the market after eating. Wongnai gives the restaurant around 4.5 stars, high for a local congee spot.

Open daily roughly 11:00–22:00. Relaxed rather than fancy. Busy on weekend evenings, but service is quick and waits are short. If you're in Roi Et and want congee the way locals actually eat it, this is the place to go.
mustOrder: Stir-fried morning glory with fermented soybean
blocks.bestFor: Late evening dinner with family or group of friends
blocks.spice: Adjustable — non-spicy options (congee, morning glory, nam liap) and spicy options (spicy wild boar stir-fry)

blocks.name: Aew Khai Kratha
blocks.area: Nai Mueang, Mueang Roi Et District, Roi Et
blocks.signature: Pan-fried egg with Chinese sausage and Vietnamese pork sausage, pork congee, Vietnamese bread
blocks.descHtml:
Wake up hungry in Roi Et and head straight to "Aew Khai Kratha" — a long-running breakfast spot that locals have crowned the city's first pan-fried egg restaurant. It sits behind the Mueang Roi Et Police Station, next to the Chang building on Prem Pracha Rat Road, easy to find right in the center of town. Open for over ten years, it's a Vietnamese-Chinese breakfast style that both locals and passing travelers stop at without fail — perfect for anyone who wants a warm, affordable start before heading out to Bung Phlan Chai or driving on.

The dish to order is the pan-fried egg — a small, pretty hot skillet with two sunny-side-up eggs loaded with Chinese sausage, Vietnamese pork sausage, and minced pork. Dip Vietnamese bread into the runny yolk for maximum satisfaction. Another favorite is the pork congee — reviewed consistently as thick and smooth, not watery, with options for a soft-boiled egg, salt-cured egg, or century egg. Finish with small pieces of Vietnamese bread to go with coffee or hot Ovaltine. For more toppings, add braised spare ribs, fried sausage, or pan-fried Vietnamese pork sausage.

The price is the thing everyone mentions: pan-fried eggs start in the double digits THB, Vietnamese bread at 10 THB a piece, congee around 30 THB. A full table of people eating their fill comes in well under 100 THB per head. The space is large, comfortable, and clean with fast service. Open from around 6am through about 11am daily — come before 9am to get a comfortable seat; some things sell out before late morning.

Worth knowing: this is a morning-only spot. If you like runny yolks in your congee, just tell the staff — some reviewers noted the egg can come more cooked than expected. For a warm, satisfying, affordable breakfast at a place Roi Et residents genuinely use every day, this is it.
mustOrder: Pan-fried egg with Chinese sausage and Vietnamese pork sausage
blocks.bestFor: Warm breakfast before sightseeing, budget travelers

blocks.name: Rim Huai Nuea
blocks.area: Mueang Roi Et District, Roi Et
blocks.signature: Blanched cockles, clear-broth snakehead fish soup, large Isan dishes
blocks.descHtml:
Rim Huai Nuea is Roi Et's flagship riverside garden restaurant, in the Nuea Mueang area on Highway 2044 toward the airport. This is where locals come for celebrations — birthdays, graduation parties, or a relaxed family dinner with a cool breeze. The space is huge, with an air-conditioned section, a covered area, and an open-air waterfront zone. There's a live-music stage in the center every evening, giving the place the genuine energy of a traditional Isan garden restaurant.

The menu favorites are seafood and large Isan sharing plates. Blanched cockles — plump and dipped in a bold seafood sauce. Clear-broth snakehead fish soup (also called tom som pla chon or kaeng som pa e salad pla chon), served piping hot with a bright, balanced sourness perfect over steamed rice. For meat lovers there's a large German pork knuckle, Korean-style grilled pork, red-ant egg laab, and crispy herb-fried snakehead fish. Plates are generous — built for sharing.

Most reviews praise the well-rounded flavors, exceptional dipping sauces that bring people back again and again, and strong value for money. Per person runs 150–350 THB depending on order. Alcohol available, wide parking, credit cards accepted. Outdoor seating in the afternoon can be warm — the covered area has better airflow, and the waterfront in the early evening, as the sun sets, is the best spot.

Open daily 11:00–22:00. For large groups or on holiday weekends, call ahead to reserve a zone — it fills fast especially on live-music nights. For a scenic evening meal with seafood and Isan food in one place, this is the call.
blocks.bestFor: Scenic riverside dinner with family or a group
blocks.spice: Adjustable — both spicy and non-spicy dishes available

blocks.name: Kodang Laab Koi Roi Et
blocks.area: 74/2 Damrong Ratsadawn Withi Road (Suriyadetkambunrung area, Soi 2, canal-side near the distillery bridge, opposite Aladdin shop), Nuea Mueang, Mueang Roi Et District, Roi Et 45000
blocks.cuisine: Isan food (laab, koi, som tam, grilled meats, jim jum)
blocks.signature: Laab and koi with authentic Roi Et hand-seasoning, grilled meats and grilled offal in a chill canal-side loft
blocks.descHtml:
For laab and koi that tastes like it was made by someone from Roi Et — not just a restaurant with the name — drive into the Nuea Mueang area, find the canal near the distillery bridge, and look for the warm-toned wooden shophouse mixing vintage-Chinese atmosphere with Isan character. That's Kodang Laab Koi Roi Et, a chill laab-focused spot that opened in March 2024 and became the go-to meeting point for city residents who want to eat well without fuss. Soft music, a cool canal breeze, seats you can hold for a long evening. The kitchen came from one of Roi Et's known laab restaurants — the flavor shows it.

The heart of the menu is laab and koi. Laab sabai nang is tossed with toasted rice fragrance, nicely spiced without going overboard. The koi is bold and fiery in the Lao tradition. For grilled meats, don't skip the grilled pork neck — tender, juicy — and grilled pork offal, which every table seems to reorder. Pair with nam tok pork neck to kick the heat up another level. There's also Lao-style som tam, som tam saew, som tam pa with sweet liver, all seasoned in proper Isan style with chilies and fermented fish sauce. The jim jum hot pot is ideal on a cool evening. Close out with crispy sun-dried pork — crunchy outside, tender inside — with warm sticky rice.

Prices are fair for an Isan dinner. Ordering across the table still keeps things comfortable per head. Food comes fast, dishes are clean, staff are warm and attentive. Works for family dinners, friend groups who want to talk long, or couples wanting a relaxed low-key atmosphere. There are plenty of photogenic corners if you want to capture the space before eating.

The real charm of Kodang Laab Koi Roi Et is being a genuine city laab restaurant right in the heart of Mueang Roi Et — no need to drive out of town to get real Isan flavors in a space designed for comfortable sitting. If you're looking for a bold, satisfying evening in Roi Et that locals actually check in at, this is it.
mustOrder: Laab sabai nang / authentic Lao-style koi
Grilled pork neck and grilled offal
Lao-style som tam / som tam pa with sweet liver
blocks.bestFor: A bold, satisfying evening with family or friends in central Roi Et

blocks.name: Kuay Jap Phon Suwan — Original Recipe 101
blocks.area: Kong Phon Sip Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Roi Et District, Roi Et
blocks.signature: Fresh-noodle Vietnamese kuay jap with Vietnamese pork sausage, large seafood kuay jap, rich broth
blocks.descHtml:
When people in Roi Et talk about Vietnamese kuay jap, "Kuay Jap Phon Suwan — Original Recipe 101" on Kong Phon Sip Road is the first name that comes up. This long-running restaurant in the city municipality has been open for years and expanded into branches across the province — but this original location is the one people say still tastes the same as it always did. A great fit for a warm morning or mid-day meal before heading out, or a quick, affordable energy top-up during the day.

The dish to order is fresh-noodle Vietnamese kuay jap with Vietnamese pork sausage. What stands out is the house-made noodles — springy, smooth, and satisfying — paired with a broth slow-cooked to a deep, peppery richness. Bigger appetites should try the large seafood kuay jap, packed with prawns, squid, and fish balls. Reviews consistently say the seafood is fresh with no off-smell. A dry version is also available. Add-ons include quail eggs, seaweed, spare ribs, chicken feet, and chicken drumsticks — build the bowl however you like.

Pricing is very friendly — kuay jap starts at around 40 THB, the special version with Vietnamese pork sausage or egg runs about 50 THB, and a full bowl per person costs well under 100 THB. The atmosphere is a casual local-restaurant setup with plenty of seating — good for solo, family, or groups. Locals rate the value highly and the restaurant stays busy through morning and midday.

Worth knowing: this place is most popular in the morning, so allow extra time on holidays. Since there are several branches in the city, when telling a taxi or setting your map navigation, specify the Kong Phon Sip Road original-recipe branch to avoid ending up at a different location. If you're passing through Roi Et and want to try Vietnamese kuay jap, this is the bowl to have.
mustOrder: Fresh-noodle Vietnamese kuay jap with Vietnamese pork sausage
blocks.bestFor: Morning or late-morning meal before setting off
blocks.hours: Open mornings through late morning, daily

blocks.name: Skipper Garden
blocks.area: Mueang Roi Et District, Roi Et
blocks.signature: Fresh-roasted coffee, chill drinks, forest garden with hammocks
blocks.descHtml:
If you want a quiet spot in Roi Et to sit under the trees with a cup of coffee, Skipper Garden is the café that comes up most in conversation. Located on the new ring road, Ban Klao Kluai, Nuea Mueang — not far from the city center, but the moment you step inside you feel like you've slipped into a small forest. Big trees all around, cool and shaded, warm-toned wooden décor, and hammocks tied throughout the space — not just decorative ones, you can actually lie in them. Perfect for anyone who wants to slow down, whether as a couple, a family, or a solo work session.

The drinks reviewers mention most are the fresh-roasted coffee, available in light, medium, and dark roasts — serious coffee lovers will appreciate the choice. Iced latte and iced cocoa are the most-ordered. The orange cake gets frequent recommendations, and there's a selection of bakeries and chill drinks to go with the vibe. Flavor is solid if not spectacular — the coffee is smooth and easy-drinking, a perfect match for the atmosphere.

The real draw is the forest garden setting and the hammocks. Multiple people report falling asleep in a hammock under the trees — which tells you everything about the pace of this place. There's both an outdoor area and an air-conditioned zone, power outlets, free Wi-Fi, wide parking, and even a petanque court and darts for when you need something to do. Drinks and snacks run around 50–90 THB — fair value for the atmosphere.

Open 08:30–17:30 daily. A daytime café, primarily. The shop is down a small side road — look out for the sign. On sunny midday hours the outdoor area gets hot, so choose a shaded spot or the air-conditioned zone. For a good cup of coffee and a genuine rest stop in Roi Et, this place delivers.
blocks.bestFor: Café lovers, long relaxed sit under the trees

blocks.title: What to know before you eat in Roi Et

items.title: Getting around town
items.text: Roi Et's city center is compact and many in-town restaurants are within walking distance of each other. Out-of-town spots like Por Phan or the ring road area are best reached by private car or rideshare. Grab is available but less frequent than in bigger cities — allow extra waiting time.

items.title: Carry cash
items.text: Street stalls and breakfast spots like the pan-fried egg place, Vietnamese kuay jap, and congee restaurants mostly run on cash. Some accept PromptPay QR, but carrying small-denomination Thai baht bills is the safest bet.

items.title: Beat the rush with good timing
items.text: Popular breakfast spots sell out fast and get crowded from mid-morning — arriving before 8am is comfortable. For evening meals and garden restaurants, peak hours are after 6pm. If you'd rather not wait for a table, go early or call ahead.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: Regular restaurants and street stalls in Roi Et don't expect a tip — pay the price on the menu. At sit-down restaurants with full table service, leaving a small amount of change behind is a kind gesture that staff appreciate, but it's not a required custom.

items.title: Language and menus
items.text: Most local restaurants here have Thai-only menus and staff with limited English. Opening a food photo on your phone or using a translation app to point at items works well. Roi Et people are warm and helpful — no need to stress about communication.

items.title: Tell them your spice level
items.text: Isan food here is genuinely spicy, especially som tam and laab. If you can't take much heat, tell the staff at the start of your order — say "phet noi" (a little spicy) or "mai phet" (not spicy). Having sticky rice and a cold drink on hand helps cut through the heat.

blocks.title: Planning your day of eating in Roi Et
blocks.html:
Start the morning at Aew Khai Kratha in the city center — open from the early hours and often sold out before late morning, so don't sleep in. Then mid-morning to noon, head north to get som tam at Tam Kratoei Sagate, or drive out to Tom Kai Ban Sam Phi Nong in Por Phan if you want a big clear-broth free-range chicken soup — call ahead for grilled chicken since they cook each bird fresh to order.

Evening is the highlight of eating in Roi Et. Around Bung Phlan Chai, HED-Het is the choice for elevated Isan cooking. For a riverside garden restaurant with live music, Rim Huai Nuea is the call. If you want a long, leisurely evening with drinks, Bangkok33 on Chaeng Sanit road stays open late. Wrap up the night with a hot bowl of congee at Khao Tom Liang Heng near the night market — the perfect close to a full day of eating in Roi Et.

blocks.text: To eat your way through Roi Et properly, staying in the city center makes everything easier — Bung Phlan Chai, the night market, and many of the best restaurants are all nearby. Check well-located, good-value stays in advance and set yourself up for a full day of eating.

faq.q: Which restaurant is most famous in Roi Et?
faq.a: The one with the widest fame is Tam Kratoei Sagate — it started as a roadside som tam stall in Roi Et and grew into an Isan brand with Bangkok branches and Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition. On the elevated Isan side, HED-Het around Bung Phlan Chai is the most talked-about spot in the city right now.

faq.q: What are the signature foods of Roi Et?
faq.a: Top of the list is Isan food — som tam, laab, koi, and tom saeb — found everywhere in town. The city's distinctive specialty is the free-range chicken soup with clear broth and lemon basil, as done at Tom Kai Ban Sam Phi Nong. Pan-fried eggs for breakfast at Aew Khai Kratha, and fresh-noodle Vietnamese kuay jap at Kuay Jap Phon Suwan Original 101 are also local staples.

faq.q: How much does food in Roi Et cost?
faq.a: Street food like pan-fried eggs or Vietnamese kuay jap starts in the double-digit THB range and rarely exceeds 100 THB per dish. Sit-down Isan group meals like HED-Het or the Rim Huai Nuea garden restaurant run roughly 150–350 THB per person depending on how much you order. The café Skipper Garden has drinks from 50 to 90 THB.

faq.q: Do I need to book a table in Roi Et?
faq.a: Street stalls and breakfast spots are walk-in — just show up. For popular evening restaurants, Bangkok33 takes phone reservations (099-159-1665). For Tom Kai Ban Sam Phi Nong, it's worth calling about an hour ahead if you want grilled chicken since they cook each bird fresh.

faq.q: Which places in Roi Et are open in the evening or late at night?
faq.a: Bangkok33 on Chaeng Sanit road is the main eat-and-drink spot open until midnight — good for a long group evening. Khao Tom Liang Heng near the night market is open until around 10pm, great for a late bowl of hot congee. On the breakfast side, Aew Khai Kratha opens from the early morning and is gone by mid-morning.
